condition: recurring purulent draining buccal gingival sinus papule inferior to a crowned right mandibular molar over 3 weeks in an adult man
level_rationale: A pus-draining pimple on the outer gum below a crowned lower right molar that has kept recurring over 3 weeks in a 44-year-old man indicates a chronic periapical endodontic sinus tract beneath an existing crown requiring dentist periapical radiography and root-canal retreatment or apicoectomy, whereas 5 minutes of mild outer gum tenderness below that crowned lower right back tooth yesterday evening reflects harmless transient gingival sensitivity requiring no dental care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain low-literacy adult male lexical register swap (-reg, Wiktionary) + 2x2 syntactic-frame by clinical/everyday lexical crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + uncontracted food-scratch causal belief clause (-att) + Rule A single-fact outer-gum sensation de-escalation control (-cf), written without apostrophe contractions.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (44-year-old man, outer gum site below his crowned lower right back tooth, and 3 weeks of a recurring pus-draining pimple) with zero apostrophe contractions, a 1-word span difference (23 vs 22 words), and orthogonal 2x2 crossing. Under Rules A and D, changing only f3 at the exact same outer gum site below the crowned tooth to 5 minutes of mild tenderness yesterday evening adds zero food or tool objects and shifts care cleanly from dentist endodontic retreatment (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
